documents.title: Receiver acknowledgement and processing SLA v2
documents.content:
# Receiver acknowledgement and processing SLA v2.1

An HTTP 202 from the receiver proves durable acceptance into its queue only. It does not by itself prove that the receiver completed business processing.

Check the receiver's current state for the same `event_id` and `delivery_version`. `PROCESSED` is sufficient to prove completion even before the SLA deadline, provided the current receiver observation is correlated to that same event and delivery version.

SLA only sets the handling direction for a same-event receiver that remains `QUEUED`: before the trusted deadline, continue observing; at or after the deadline, contact the receiver operator to investigate. An overdue `QUEUED` state does not by itself prove business failure or event loss.

HTTP 202 alone proves acceptance only; without current same-event receiver evidence, the processing state is `UNKNOWN`. Do not infer the target event's state from elapsed time, a different event, an order snapshot, or historical advice. Never resend automatically.

documents.title: Order lifecycle and asynchronous event publication v2
documents.content: Protocol v2. HTTP 200 confirms only that the bound order read succeeded. Callback creation follows the terminal COMPLETED transition, but event publication can be asynchronous. Correlate the event's order version to the current bound order and inspect a delivery attempt before attributing a missing callback to transport failure. Do not treat PROCESSING as a callback incident.

documents.title: Callback failure classification and retry policy v2
documents.content: Protocol v2 error handling. A 503 response is retriable only when the server records a retryable failure code and a current retry policy. Retry state SCHEDULED with retry_at is still pending. EXHAUSTED is actionable only when attempt_count reaches max_attempts and the failure response digest/event/request all match the current delivery row. This document describes method; current Domain Evidence decides the incident.
